title: AJCC Certification and Local Plan Evidence Workshop
description: A deadline-driven workshop for the current certification and planning cycle. Focuses on certification indicator #6 ("high-quality, well-informed, and cross-trained staff") and the staff-training narrative required in local plan modifications due April 30, 2027. Learners leave with a draft evidence package and plan language.
notes: Audience: Board staff, operators, managers. Format: HD (offered before May 15, 2027). Hours assumed from format (HD = 4 hours).
learning_objectives: Interpret the seven certification indicators under WSD25-05 and what evidence each needs.
Assemble a cross-training evidence package for indicator #6.
Draft the frontline staff training section of a local plan modification.
Turn certification findings into a Continuous Improvement Plan with training actions.

lessons.title: Project: Draft Evidence Package and Plan Language

sequencing_rationale: Lessons follow the catalog's learning objectives in the order a practitioner meets them on the job: The Seven Certification Indicators and Their Evidence; Building the Indicator #6 Evidence Package; Drafting the Staff Training Section of the Local Plan Modification; From Findings to a Continuous Improvement Plan. The closing project ("Project: Draft Evidence Package and Plan Language") applies the earlier lessons to one realistic work product (a draft indicator #6 evidence package, local plan training language, and a Continuous Improvement Plan with training actions) rather than introducing new content. Scope assumptions: hours are not stated in the source catalog and are assumed from the delivery format (HD (offered before May 15, 2027); HD = 4 hours). Content is grounded in California and federal guidance named in the catalog description and objectives; the course cites those directives by number but does not reproduce their text, and every policy-specific claim must be checked against the current directive before delivery. Local board policy is treated as a variable the learner fills in from their own board, not something the course prescribes.
